newsitem.title: UK: UK SFA says considering NatWest report.
newsitem.headline: UK SFA says considering NatWest report.

text.p: Britain's financial markets watchdog, the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA), said on Thursday it had received a copy of a report into options losses at NatWest Markets and would study it before making any moves.
It is within the SFA's power to discipline firms and individuals if they are proved to have contravened its rules.
NatWest Markets, the investment banking unit of National Westminster Bank Plc, has booked 77 million stg of losses which it admitted had been caused by poor trading and adverse market conditions.

It said the report, prepared by law firm Linklaters & Paines and accountants Coopers & Lybrand, shows the losses were covered up over two years by deliberate mis-pricing and over-valuing and by false adjustments in pricing models.
NatWest also said that unauthorised transfers of value had taken place between options books and that all of these were facilitated by weak controls at the bank.
An SFA spokesman said it might need to supplement the findings of the report with its own enquiries, adding that it should be in a position to announce any action soon.
